Rule DORA-07: Digital operational resilience testing
Requirement: A risk-based digital operational resilience testing programme is run, with critical systems tested at least yearly; significant entities also perform threat-led penetration testing at least every three years (Art. 24-26).
Problem found: gap in section 'Resilience testing'
Evidence (redacted): There is no fixed testing programme, and the card authorisation and settlement systems have not had a penetration test in the last three years.
Hint from the rule owner: Set up a yearly testing programme for critical ICT systems and plan threat-led penetration testing every three years if the entity is significant.

Rule DORA-09: Exit strategies for critical ICT providers
Requirement: For ICT services that support critical or important functions, documented and tested exit strategies exist so the entity can leave a provider without disruption (Art. 28(8)).
Problem found: gap in section 'Exit from ICT providers'
Evidence (redacted): No exit plan has been written or tested; the team will work one out if a provider ever has to be replaced.
Hint from the rule owner: Write and test an exit plan for each ICT provider that supports a critical or important function.

Rule DORA-01: Management body owns ICT risk
Requirement: The management body defines, approves and oversees the ICT risk management framework and bears final responsibility for it (Art. 5).
Problem found: gap in section 'Governance'
Evidence (redacted): The Head of IT Operations owns this policy and approves changes.
Hint from the rule owner: State that the management body approves the ICT risk management framework, reviews it at least yearly and is accountable for it.

Rule DORA-02: Documented ICT risk management framework
Requirement: A documented ICT risk management framework covers strategies, policies, procedures and tools to protect ICT assets, and is reviewed at least once a year and after major incidents (Art. 6).
Problem found: possible gap in section 'Governance' below the 0.75 confidence threshold
Evidence (redacted): The policy is reviewed when the IT department considers it necessary.
Hint from the rule owner: Describe the ICT risk management framework and commit to a review at least once a year and after every major ICT incident.

Rule DORA-04: Major ICT incidents classified and reported
Requirement: ICT-related incidents are recorded and classified; major incidents are reported to the competent authority with an initial notification, an intermediate report and a final report within the deadlines of the reporting technical standards (Art. 17-19).
Problem found: gap in section 'Incident classification'
Evidence (redacted): Every ICT incident is logged in the service desk tool and given a priority from P1 to P4 based on the number of affected customers and the duration of the outage.
Hint from the rule owner: Add an incident classification scheme and a procedure to send initial, intermediate and final reports of major ICT incidents to the competent authority on the regulatory deadlines.

Rule DORA-04: Major ICT incidents classified and reported
Requirement: ICT-related incidents are recorded and classified; major incidents are reported to the competent authority with an initial notification, an intermediate report and a final report within the deadlines of the reporting technical standards (Art. 17-19).
Problem found: gap in section 'Incident classification'
Evidence (redacted): Every ICT incident is logged in the service desk tool and given a priority from P1 to P4 based on the number of affected customers and the duration of the outage.
Hint from the rule owner: Add an incident classification scheme and a procedure to send initial, intermediate and final reports of major ICT incidents to the competent authority on the regulatory deadlines.
<thinking>Based on the rule and the evidence, the current system only assigns a priority to incidents based on the number of affected customers and the duration of the outage. However, it lacks a formal incident classification scheme and a procedure for reporting major incidents to the competent authority. To meet the requirement, I need to propose a concrete fix that includes both an incident classification scheme and a reporting procedure for major incidents.</thinking>

<thinking>I will now propose a concrete fix that includes both an incident classification scheme and a reporting procedure for major incidents.</thinking>

{"fix": "Implement an incident classification scheme that categorizes incidents into levels such as Critical, High, Medium, and Low. Ensure that all major incidents (Critical and High) are reported to the competent authority with an initial notification within 24 hours, an intermediate report within 72 hours, and a final report within 30 days. This will ensure compliance with the reporting technical standards."}
[{"text": "Fix recorded."}]

Rule DORA-05: ICT business continuity with tested recovery
Requirement: An ICT business continuity policy with response and recovery plans exists, sets recovery objectives, and the plans are tested regularly (Art. 11).
Problem found: gap in section 'Business continuity'
Evidence (redacted): The recovery plan was last exercised in 2023.
Hint from the rule owner: Define recovery time and recovery point objectives for critical functions and test the recovery plans at least yearly.

Rule DORA-06: Backups and restoration tested
Requirement: Backup policies define scope and frequency based on criticality, and restoration from backups is tested periodically, using systems segregated from the source (Art. 12).
Problem found: possible gap in section 'Backups' below the 0.75 confidence threshold
Evidence (redacted): Production databases are backed up every night to a separate data centre.
Hint from the rule owner: Define what is backed up and how often per criticality, keep backups segregated, and test restores on a fixed schedule.

Rule DORA-06: Backups and restoration tested
Requirement: Backup policies define scope and frequency based on criticality, and restoration from backups is tested periodically, using systems segregated from the source (Art. 12).
Problem found: possible gap in section 'Backups' below the 0.75 confidence threshold
Evidence (redacted): Production databases are backed up every night to a separate data centre.
Hint from the rule owner: Define what is backed up and how often per criticality, keep backups segregated, and test restores on a fixed schedule.
<thinking>The architecture rule gap concerns the lack of explicit definitions for what is backed up, how often, and the criticality level of these backups. Additionally, the rule emphasizes the segregation of backup storage and the periodic testing of restores. The evidence mentions that production databases are backed up nightly to a separate data center, but it does not specify the scope, frequency based on criticality, or the testing of restorations. Therefore, I need to address these points in my fix.</thinking>

{"fix": "Define backup policies that specify what is backed up and the frequency based on the criticality of the data. Ensure that backups are stored in a segregated system from the production environment. Implement a periodic testing schedule for restoration from these backups to ensure data integrity and availability."}
[{"text": "Fix recorded."}]

Rule DORA-08: ICT third-party risk and register
Requirement: ICT third-party risk is managed under a strategy and policy; a register of information on all contractual arrangements with ICT third-party service providers is maintained (Art. 28).
Problem found: possible gap in section 'Third-party providers' below the 0.75 confidence threshold
Evidence (redacted): Card processing and cloud hosting are outsourced to external ICT providers.
Hint from the rule owner: Adopt an ICT third-party risk policy and keep a register of information covering every ICT service contract.
